title: Water Inlet Fault
shortDescription: Dishwasher is not filling with water within the allowed time.
fullDescription:
E01 indicates that the dishwasher did not detect enough water entering the tub within the timeout window. Typical causes are a closed supply tap, a blocked inlet filter, or a failed inlet valve.

On Grundig models (Arcelik platform, shared with Beko and Blomberg) also check the aqua-stop hose — a tripped aqua-stop blocks flow and flags E01.

causes.cause: Closed or partially closed supply tap

fixSteps.title: Open supply tap
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure cold water tap is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet filter
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect hose at rear and clean filter mesh.

whenToCallPro: If valve replacement does not resolve.

faq.q: Will cleaning the filter fix it?
faq.a: Often yes — the inlet mesh clogs with limescale.

title: Drain Fault
shortDescription: Dishwasher is not draining water within expected time.
fullDescription: E02 indicates the drain pump cannot evacuate water from the tub — blocked filter, kinked drain hose, or a seized pump impeller are the usual causes.
symptoms: Water in tub at end of cycle

fixSteps.title: Clean filters
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and rinse the sump filters.

fixSteps.title: Check pump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pump cover and clear debris from impeller.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new drain pump if impeller free but pump silent.

whenToCallPro: If debris is in sealed sump.

title: Heater / NTC Fault
shortDescription: Water not heating or temperature sensor faulty.
fullDescription: E03 is raised when the dishwasher fails to heat the water within the expected time, or the NTC sensor reports an impossible value. Flow-through heaters, NTC, and TOC are the usual suspects.

title: Overflow / Aqua-Stop Triggered
shortDescription: Overflow switch in base tray has tripped.
fullDescription: E04 indicates water detected in the anti-flood base tray. The dishwasher will run the drain pump continuously and refuse to start new cycles until dried out.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect and tip
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power, tip machine forward to drain tray.

fixSteps.title: Find leak
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect hoses, door seal, and sump for leaks.

title: Wash Pump / Circulation Fault
shortDescription: Circulation pump is not running correctly.
fullDescription: E05 means the circulation (wash) pump cannot reach expected speed. Jammed impeller from debris or a failed motor are the typical causes.
whenToCallPro: Pump replacement often needs tilt/seal work.

title: Turbidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Optical soil sensor reports invalid reading.
fullDescription: E06 indicates the turbidity (optical) sensor is faulty or its lens is heavily fouled with detergent residue. Cleaning often resolves the issue without a part.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sump cover and wipe optical sensor lens.

title: Flow Meter Fault
shortDescription: Inlet flow meter reports no pulses.
fullDescription: E07 indicates the flow meter (water quantity sensor) is not producing pulses despite water entering. Limescale in the flow meter paddle wheel is the most common cause.

title: Diverter Valve Fault
shortDescription: Spray arm diverter cannot reach position.
fullDescription: E08 indicates the spray arm diverter motor cannot find its position. Debris jam or failed motor are usual causes.

title: Control Board Error
fullDescription: E09 is a generic PCB fault code — firmware corruption, relay failure, or a communication breakdown with peripheral boards. Power cycle first; persistent E09 needs board replacement.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: Door latch switch not confirming closed state.
fullDescription: E10 means the door switch circuit is open during cycle. Loose latch, worn microswitch, or broken wiring are the usual culprits.
